title: Ukrainian National Assembly – Ukrainian National Self Defence
aliases: Українська Національна Асамблея — Українська Народна Самооборона
summary: The Ukrainian National Assembly – Ukrainian People's Self-Defence (UNA-UNSO) is a Ukrainian nationalist organization comprising a political wing and a paramilitary wing. Established in 1991, it has played a significant role in far-right politics in Ukraine and has participated in various international conflicts.

sections.heading: Formation and Early Years
paragraphs: The [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] National Assembly was founded on 30 June 1990 in [[lviv|Lviv]] as the Ukrainian Interparty Assembly. Following a congress in [[kyiv|Kyiv]] in November 1990, the organization evolved, and by 19 August 1991, it had formed squads of the [[ukrainians|Ukrainian People]]'s Self-Defense in response to the Soviet coup attempt. The organization was officially renamed the Ukrainian National Assembly – Ukrainian National Self-Defence after [[ukraine|Ukraine]]'s Declaration of Independence on 8 September 1991.

sections.heading: Political Activities and Influence
paragraphs: The UNA-UNSO was registered as a political party in December 1994, and during the 1994 parliamentary elections, three of its members were elected to the [[verkhovna-rada|Verkhovna Rada]]. The organization gained notoriety for its anti-Russian activities, including the destruction of a Russian flag in parliament and participation in the First Chechen War alongside Chechen rebels. By the late 1990s, membership peaked at around 10,000, primarily among younger individuals.

sections.heading: International Conflicts
paragraphs: UNA-UNSO members have participated in several international conflicts, including the [[transnistria|Transnistria]] War, the War in [[republic-of-abkhazia|Abkhazia]], and the [[full-scale-russo-ukrainian-war|Russo-Ukrainian War]]. During the Transnistria War, they fought alongside separatists, while in Abkhazia, they supported Georgian forces against Russian-backed separatists. In the ongoing Russo-Ukrainian War, UNSO has been involved as part of various volunteer battalions.

sections.heading: Leadership and Structure
paragraphs: The leadership of the UNA-UNSO has changed over the years, with notable leaders including Yuriy Shukhevych and Andriy Shkil. Following a ban imposed by the government in 1997, members responded with protests, and the organization has since undergone various transformations, including a merger with Right Sector in May 2014.

sections.heading: Ideology and Image
paragraphs: The UNA-UNSO's ideology has been characterized as nationalist, envisioning Kyiv as the center of a pan-Slavic military bloc. Despite being described as a fringe movement, its visibility has had a notable impact on far-right politics [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]]. The organization's anthem is a rendition of 'Bella ciao'.
